sanskrit: divyajñānaḥ sa tejasvī jñātvā taṃ nṛpatiṃ tadā kṣīṇāyuṣaṃ pāṇḍaveyam apāvartata kāśyapaḥ labdhvā vittaṃ munivaras takṣakād yāvad īpsitam
english: That brilliant one endowed with divine knowledge, having understood that the king, the descendant of Pāṇḍu, had then exhausted his span of life, the sage Kāśyapa turned back — having obtained from Takṣaka as much wealth as he desired.

sanskrit: nivṛtte kāśyape tasmin samayena mahātmani jagāma takṣakas tūrṇaṃ nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: When that great-souled Kāśyapa had turned away at that moment, Takṣaka swiftly went to the city named after the serpents — Hastināpura.

sanskrit: atha śuśrāva gacchan sa takṣako jagatīpatim mantrāgadair viṣaharai rakṣyamāṇaṃ prayatnataḥ
english: And as he went, Takṣaka heard that the lord of the earth was being carefully protected by means of charms, antidotes, and poison-neutralizing medicines.

sanskrit: sa cintayām āsa tadā māyāyogena pārthivaḥ mayā vañcayitavyo 'sau ka upāyo bhaved iti
english: He then reflected: "By what stratagem of illusion can I deceive this king? What means might there be?"

sanskrit: tatas tāpasarūpeṇa prāhiṇot sa bhujaṃgamān phalapatrodakaṃ gṛhya rājñe nāgo 'tha takṣakaḥ
english: Then the serpent Takṣaka, taking fruits, leaves, and water, sent other snakes in the guise of ascetics to the king.

sanskrit: takṣaka uvāca gacchadhvaṃ yūyam avyagrā rājānaṃ kāryavattayā phalapatrodakaṃ nāma pratigrāhayituṃ nṛpam
english: Takṣaka said: "Go to the king calmly, on the pretext of a mission, and have the king accept these — fruits, leaves, and water."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca te takṣakasamādiṣṭās tathā cakrur bhujaṃgamāḥ upaninyus tathā rājñe darbhān āpaḥ phalāni ca
english: The Sūta said: Those snakes, instructed by Takṣaka, did exactly so — they presented to the king darbha grass, water, and fruits.

sanskrit: tac ca sarvaṃ sa rājendraḥ pratijagrāha vīryavān kṛtvā ca teṣāṃ kāryāṇi gamyatām ity uvāca tān
english: The mighty king of kings accepted all of it, and having attended to their business, he said to them: "You may go."

sanskrit: gateṣu teṣu nāgeṣu tāpasacchadmarūpiṣu amātyān suhṛdaś caiva provāca sa narādhipaḥ
english: When those snakes in the disguise of ascetics had departed, the lord of men spoke to his ministers and friends.

sanskrit: bhakṣayantu bhavanto vai svādūnīmāni sarvaśaḥ tāpasair upanītāni phalāni sahitā mayā
english: "Let all of you eat these sweet fruits that the ascetics have brought — together with me."

sanskrit: tato rājā sasacivaḥ phalāny ādātum aicchata yad gṛhītaṃ phalaṃ rājñā tatra kṛmir abhūd aṇuḥ hrasvakaḥ kṛṣṇanayanas tāmro varṇena śaunaka
english: Then the king along with his minister went to take the fruits. In the fruit taken by the king there appeared a tiny worm — small, dark-eyed, and copper-colored, O Śaunaka.

sanskrit: sa taṃ gṛhya nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ sacivān idam abravīt astam abhyeti savitā viṣād adya na me bhayam
english: Taking it up, that foremost of kings said to his ministers: "The sun is setting; today I no longer have any fear of poison."

sanskrit: satyavāg astu sa muniḥ kṛmiko māṃ daśatv ayam takṣako nāma bhūtvā vai tathā parihṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "Let that sage's words prove true — let this little worm bite me, becoming Takṣaka by name; in that way the prophecy shall be fulfilled."

sanskrit: te cainam anvavartanta mantriṇaḥ kālacoditāḥ evam uktvā sa rājendro grīvāyāṃ saṃniveśya ha kṛmikaṃ prāhasat tūrṇaṃ mumūrṣur naṣṭacetanaḥ
english: And those ministers followed his lead, driven by fate. Having spoken thus, that king of kings placed the little worm on his neck, laughed aloud, and swiftly he who was near death lost consciousness.

sanskrit: hasann eva ca bhogena takṣakeṇābhiveṣṭitaḥ tasmāt phalād viniṣkramya yat tad rājñe niveditam
english: Still laughing, he was coiled by Takṣaka in serpent form, who had emerged from that very fruit — the one that had been presented to the king.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca taṃ tathā mantriṇo dṛṣṭvā bhogena pariveṣṭitam vivarṇavadanāḥ sarve rurudur bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: The Sūta said: Seeing him thus encoiled by the serpent, all the ministers, their faces gone pale, wept, overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: taṃ tu nādaṃ tataḥ śrutvā mantriṇas te pradudruvuḥ apaśyaṃś caiva te yāntam ākāśe nāgam adbhutam
english: Hearing that cry, those ministers fled in all directions, and they saw the wondrous serpent moving through the sky.

sanskrit: sīmantam iva kurvāṇaṃ nabhasaḥ padmavarcasam takṣakaṃ pannagaśreṣṭhaṃ bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Overwhelmed with sorrow, they saw Takṣaka, that foremost of serpents, of lotus-like radiance, streaking across the sky as if parting it in two.

sanskrit: tatas tu te tad gṛham agninā vṛtaṃ; pradīpyamānaṃ viṣajena bhoginaḥ bhayāt parityajya diśaḥ prapedire; papāta tac cāśanitāḍitaṃ yathā
english: Then, as the serpent's venom set the palace ablaze and it burned, they abandoned it in fear and fled in all directions; and it fell like a tree struck by lightning.

sanskrit: tato nṛpe takṣakatejasā hate; prayujya sarvāḥ paralokasatkriyāḥ śucir dvijo rājapurohitas tadā; tathaiva te tasya nṛpasya mantriṇaḥ
english: When the king was slain by the power of Takṣaka, the pure brahmin who was the royal chaplain, and likewise all the ministers of that king, performed all the rites for the other world.

sanskrit: nṛpaṃ śiśuṃ tasya sutaṃ pracakrire; sametya sarve puravāsino janāḥ nṛpaṃ yam āhus tam amitraghātinaṃ; kurupravīraṃ janamejayaṃ janāḥ
english: All the people of the city assembled and made his young son king — that hero of the Kurus whom they called the destroyer of enemies: Janamejaya.

sanskrit: sa bāla evāryamatir nṛpottamaḥ; sahaiva tair mantripurohitais tadā śaśāsa rājyaṃ kurupuṃgavāgrajo; yathāsya vīraḥ prapitāmahas tathā
english: Even as a child, that foremost of kings, noble-minded and pre-eminent among the bulls of the Kuru line, governed the kingdom together with those ministers and the royal priest, just as his valiant great-grandfather had done.

sanskrit: tatas tu rājānam amitratāpanaṃ; samīkṣya te tasya nṛpasya mantriṇaḥ suvarṇavarmāṇam upetya kāśipaṃ; vapuṣṭamārthaṃ varayāṃ pracakramuḥ
english: Then the ministers of that king, seeing him as the scorcher of enemies, approached the Kāśi king Suvarṇavarman and sued for Vapuṣṭamā on his behalf.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā pradadau vapuṣṭamāṃ; kurupravīrāya parīkṣya dharmataḥ sa cāpi tāṃ prāpya mudā yuto 'bhavan; na cānyanārīṣu mano dadhe kva cit
english: Then that king, having examined the match by dharmic standards, gave Vapuṣṭamā to that hero of the Kurus; and the hero, having obtained her, was filled with joy, and never again set his mind on any other woman.

sanskrit: saraḥsu phulleṣu vaneṣu caiva ha; prasannacetā vijahāra vīryavān tathā sa rājanyavaro vijahrivān; yathorvaśīṃ prāpya purā purūravāḥ
english: The valiant one sported with a cheerful heart in lakes full of blooms and in forests; that best of kings disported himself just as Purūravas of old had done upon obtaining Urvaśī.

sanskrit: vapuṣṭamā cāpi varaṃ patiṃ tadā; pratītarūpaṃ samavāpya bhūmipam bhāvena rāmā ramayāṃ babhūva vai; vihārakāleṣv avarodhasundarī
english: And Vapuṣṭamā too, having obtained that excellent and handsome lord of the earth as husband, delighted him with her love; that beauty of the inner quarters was his joy in all his hours of pleasure.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu jaratkārur mahātapāḥ cacāra pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ yatrasāyaṃgṛho muniḥ
english: The Sūta said: At this very time, the sage Jaratkāru of great austerities, who had no fixed home, wandered over the entire earth, sleeping wherever evening found him.

sanskrit: caran dīkṣāṃ mahātejā duścarām akṛtātmabhiḥ tīrtheṣv āplavanaṃ kurvan puṇyeṣu vicacāra ha
english: Of great splendor, practising a severe vow of initiation impossible for the undisciplined, he wandered among sacred tirthas, bathing at each holy site.

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣo nirāhāraḥ śuṣyann aharahar muniḥ sa dadarśa pitṝn garte lambamānān adhomukhān
english: Living on air alone, taking no food, the sage drying up day by day — he saw his ancestors hanging head-downward in a pit.

sanskrit: ekatantvavaśiṣṭaṃ vai vīraṇastambam āśritān taṃ ca tantuṃ śanair ākhum ādadānaṃ bilāśrayam
english: They were clinging to a clump of vīraṇa grass of which only a single stalk remained, and a rat that lived in the burrow below was slowly gnawing at that stalk.

sanskrit: nirāhārān kṛśān dīnān garte ''rtāṃs trāṇam icchataḥ upasṛtya sa tān dīnān dīnarūpo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Those without food, emaciated and wretched, hanging in the pit and longing for rescue — he approached those miserable ones, himself appearing wretched, and addressed them.

sanskrit: ke bhavanto 'valambante vīraṇastambam āśritāḥ durbalaṃ khāditair mūlair ākhunā bilavāsinā
english: "Who are you, clinging to this clump of vīraṇa grass, now weak because its roots are being eaten by the rat that dwells in the burrow?"

sanskrit: vīraṇastambake mūlaṃ yad apy ekam iha sthitam tad apy ayaṃ śanair ākhur ādatte daśanaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: "Even the one root of this vīraṇa clump that still remains here, this rat is slowly taking away with its sharp teeth."

sanskrit: chetsyate 'lpāvaśiṣṭatvād etad apy acirād iva tataḥ stha patitāro 'tra garte asminn adhomukhāḥ
english: "Because so little remains, even this will be severed before long; then you will fall head-downward into this very pit."

sanskrit: tato me duḥkham utpannaṃ dṛṣṭvā yuṣmān adhomukhān kṛcchrām āpadam āpannān priyaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ
english: "Seeing you hanging head-downward and fallen into this dire calamity, grief has arisen in me. What good may I do for you?"

sanskrit: tapaso 'sya caturthena tṛtīyenāpi vā punaḥ ardhena vāpi nistartum āpadaṃ brūta māciram
english: "Tell me without delay whether I can rescue you from this calamity with a quarter, or a third, or even half of my austerities."

sanskrit: athavāpi samagreṇa tarantu tapasā mama bhavantaḥ sarva evāsmāt kāmam evaṃ vidhīyatām
english: "Or perhaps all of you may cross over this difficulty by means of the whole of my austerities — let it be arranged as you wish."

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ ṛddho bhavān brahmacārī yo nas trātum ihecchati na tu viprāgrya tapasā śakyam etad vyapohitum
english: The ancestors said: You are a prosperous celibate student who desires to save us here; but, O foremost of brahmins, this cannot be removed by austerity alone.

sanskrit: asti nas tāta tapasaḥ phalaṃ pravadatāṃ vara saṃtānaprakṣayād brahman patāmo niraye 'śucau
english: "We have the fruit of our austerities, O son, O best among the eloquent; but, O brahmin, we are falling into an impure hell because our lineage is dying out."

sanskrit: lambatām iha nas tāta na jñānaṃ pratibhāti vai yena tvāṃ nābhijānīmo loke vikhyātapauruṣam
english: "As we hang here, O son, understanding does not come to us — we do not recognize you, though your valor is renowned in the world."

sanskrit: ṛddho bhavān mahābhāgo yo naḥ śocyān suduḥkhitān śocasy upetya kāruṇyāc chṛṇu ye vai vayaṃ dvija
english: "You are prosperous and greatly blessed; out of compassion you have come and grieve for us who are pitiable and deeply pained. Hear who we are, O brahmin."

sanskrit: yāyāvarā nāma vayam ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ lokāt puṇyād iha bhraṣṭāḥ saṃtānaprakṣayād vibho
english: "We are the sages called the Yāyāvaras, of sharp vows; we have fallen from the meritorious worlds into this place because our line is dying, O lord."

sanskrit: pranaṣṭaṃ nas tapaḥ puṇyaṃ na hi nas tantur asti vai asti tv eko 'dya nas tantuḥ so 'pi nāsti yathā tathā
english: "Our meritorious austerities are being destroyed, for we have no thread of lineage. There is one thread left to us today, yet it is as good as gone."

sanskrit: mandabhāgyo 'lpabhāgyānāṃ bandhuḥ sa kila naḥ kule jaratkārur iti khyāto vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ niyatātmā mahātmā ca suvrataḥ sumahātapāḥ
english: "He who is the kinsman of the wretched in our family is himself unfortunate — known as Jaratkāru, versed in the Vedas and their auxiliaries, self-controlled, great-souled, of excellent vows, and of very great austerities."

sanskrit: tena sma tapaso lobhāt kṛcchram āpāditā vayam na tasya bhāryā putro vā bāndhavo vāsti kaś cana
english: "By his greed for austerity we have been brought to this calamity. He has no wife, no son, no kinsman whatsoever."

sanskrit: tasmāl lambāmahe garte naṣṭasaṃjñā hy anāthavat sa vaktavyas tvayā dṛṣṭvā asmākaṃ nāthavattayā
english: "That is why we hang in this pit, our senses lost, like those without a protector. You, having seen our plight, should speak to him on our behalf so that we may have a guardian."

sanskrit: pitaras te 'valambante garte dīnā adhomukhāḥ sādhu dārān kuruṣveti prajāyasveti cābhibho kulatantur hi naḥ śiṣṭas tvam evaikas tapodhana
english: "'Your fathers hang wretched and head-downward in a pit — take a wife and beget offspring, O lord.' For you alone, O wealth of austerity, remain as the single thread of our lineage."

sanskrit: yaṃ tu paśyasi no brahman vīraṇastambam āśritān eṣo 'smākaṃ kulastamba āsīt svakulavardhanaḥ
english: "This clump of vīraṇa grass to which you see us clinging, O brahmin — this was our family-stalk, the one that was to have enlarged our line."

sanskrit: yāni paśyasi vai brahman mūlānīhāsya vīrudhaḥ ete nas tantavas tāta kālena paribhakṣitāḥ
english: "These roots of this plant that you see here, O brahmin — these are our lineage-threads, O son, consumed by time."

sanskrit: yat tv etat paśyasi brahman mūlam asyārdhabhakṣitam tatra lambāmahe sarve so 'py ekas tapa āsthitaḥ
english: "And that root of it which you see half-gnawed away — to that we all cling; he too is the sole one, and he has taken to austerity."

sanskrit: yam ākhuṃ paśyasi brahman kāla eṣa mahābalaḥ sa taṃ taporataṃ mandaṃ śanaiḥ kṣapayate tudan jaratkāruṃ tapolubdhaṃ mandātmānam acetasam
english: "The rat you see, O brahmin — that is mighty Time itself; it slowly gnaws and wears away that one devoted to austerities — Jaratkāru, the witless, small-minded one, whose mind is consumed by his greed for austerity."

sanskrit: na hi nas tat tapas tasya tārayiṣyati sattama chinnamūlān paribhraṣṭān kālopahatacetasaḥ narakapratiṣṭhān paśyāsmān yathā duṣkṛtinas tathā
english: "For his austerity will not save us, O noble one — we whose roots are cut, who are utterly fallen, whose minds are struck by Time; behold us, destined for hell as though we were evildoers."

sanskrit: asmāsu patiteṣv atra saha pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ chinnaḥ kālena so 'py atra gantā vai narakaṃ tataḥ
english: "When we have fallen here along with the forefathers before us, he too, cut off by Time, will then go to hell."

sanskrit: tapo vāpy athavā yajño yac cānyat pāvanaṃ mahat tat sarvaṃ na samaṃ tāta saṃtatyeti satāṃ matam
english: "Austerity, or sacrifice, or whatever other great purification there may be — none of it equals progeny: such is the opinion of the good, O son."

sanskrit: sa tāta dṛṣṭvā brūyās tvaṃ jaratkāruṃ tapasvinam yathādṛṣṭam idaṃ cāsmai tvayākhyeyam aśeṣataḥ
english: "Having seen this, O son, you should speak to the ascetic Jaratkāru; and what you have seen here must be told to him in full."

sanskrit: yathā dārān prakuryāt sa putrāṃś cotpādayed yathā tathā brahmaṃs tvayā vācyaḥ so 'smākaṃ nāthavattayā
english: "So that he may take a wife and beget sons — in that manner, O brahmin, you must address him on our behalf, that we may have a guardian."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etac chrutvā jaratkārur duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇaḥ uvāca svān pitṝn duḥkhād bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā
english: The Sūta said: Hearing this, Jaratkāru, overwhelmed with pain and sorrow, spoke to his own ancestors in a voice choked with tears out of grief.

sanskrit: aham eva jaratkāruḥ kilbiṣī bhavatāṃ sutaḥ tad daṇḍaṃ dhārayata me duṣkṛter akṛtātmanaḥ
english: "I am that very Jaratkāru — the sinful son who is your offspring. Mete out your punishment to me, the ill-doer, the undisciplined one."

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ putra diṣṭyāsi saṃprāpta imaṃ deśaṃ yadṛcchayā kimarthaṃ ca tvayā brahman na kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ
english: The ancestors said: O son, by good fortune you have arrived at this place by chance. But why, O brahmin, have you not taken a wife?

sanskrit: jaratkārur uvāca mamāyaṃ pitaro nityaṃ hṛdy arthaḥ parivartate ūrdhvaretāḥ śarīraṃ vai prāpayeyam amutra vai
english: Jaratkāru said: This thought, O fathers, has always revolved in my heart: as an upward-semened celibate I would convey this body to the next world.

sanskrit: evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu bhavataḥ śakuntān iva lambataḥ mayā nivartitā buddhir brahmacaryāt pitāmahāḥ
english: "But having seen you hanging thus like birds, O forefathers, my mind has been turned away from celibacy."

sanskrit: kariṣye vaḥ priyaṃ kāmaṃ nivekṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ sanāmnīṃ yady ahaṃ kanyām upalapsye kadā cana
english: "I will do what you wish and take a wife — there is no doubt in this — if ever I shall find a maiden who shares my name."

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati ca yā kā cid bhaikṣavat svayam udyatā pratigrahītā tām asmi na bhareyaṃ ca yām aham
english: "And she who is freely offered, as if in alms — I will accept her; but one whom I would have to maintain, her I will not take."

sanskrit: evaṃvidham ahaṃ kuryāṃ niveśaṃ prāpnuyāṃ yadi anyathā na kariṣye tu satyam etat pitāmahāḥ
english: "If I can find such a match, I will enter householder life; otherwise I will not — this is my truth, O forefathers."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktvā tu sa pitṝṃś cacāra pṛthivīṃ muniḥ na ca sma labhate bhāryāṃ vṛddho 'yam iti śaunaka
english: The Sūta said: Having thus spoken to his ancestors, the sage wandered the earth; yet he found no wife, O Śaunaka, for people said: "This one is too old."

sanskrit: yadā nirvedam āpannaḥ pitṛbhiś coditas tathā tadāraṇyaṃ sa gatvoccaiś cukrośa bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: When he had fallen into despondency, yet urged on by his ancestors as well, he went into a forest and cried out loudly in deep anguish.

sanskrit: yāni bhūtāni santīha sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca antarhitāni vā yāni tāni śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ
english: "Whatever beings there are in this place — moving or unmoving, or those that are hidden — let them hear my words."

sanskrit: ugre tapasi vartantaṃ pitaraś codayanti mām niviśasveti duḥkhārtās teṣāṃ priyacikīrṣayā
english: "My ancestors, though I abide in fierce austerity, urge me in their distress: 'Take a wife.' Desiring to do what is dear to them, I speak."

sanskrit: niveśārthy akhilāṃ bhūmiṃ kanyābhaikṣaṃ carāmi bhoḥ daridro duḥkhaśīlaś ca pitṛbhiḥ saṃniyojitaḥ
english: "I wander the entire earth seeking a maiden given as alms for the purpose of establishing a household; I am a poor man, of a sorrowful nature, set to this task by my ancestors."

sanskrit: yasya kanyāsti bhūtasya ye mayeha prakīrtitāḥ te me kanyāṃ prayacchantu carataḥ sarvatodiśam
english: "Whatever being has a maiden among those I have here proclaimed — let them give her to me as I roam in all directions."

sanskrit: mama kanyā sanāmnī yā bhaikṣavac codyatā bhavet bhareyaṃ caiva yāṃ nāhaṃ tāṃ me kanyāṃ prayacchata
english: "Let them give me that maiden who shares my name and who is offered as if in alms, and whom I will not have to maintain — give me that maiden."

sanskrit: tatas te pannagā ye vai jaratkārau samāhitāḥ tām ādāya pravṛttiṃ te vāsukeḥ pratyavedayan
english: Then the serpents who were attentive to Jaratkāru's affairs took that intelligence and reported it to Vāsuki.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śrutvā sa nāgendraḥ kanyāṃ tāṃ samalaṃkṛtām pragṛhyāraṇyam agamat samīpaṃ tasya pannagaḥ
english: Hearing their report, that lord of serpents took that maiden adorned with ornaments and went with her into the forest, to the vicinity of that sage.

sanskrit: tatra tāṃ bhaikṣavat kanyāṃ prādāt tasmai mahātmane nāgendro vāsukir brahman na sa tāṃ pratyagṛhṇata
english: There Vāsuki, the king of serpents, offered that maiden to that great-souled one as if in alms; but O brahmin, he did not accept her.

sanskrit: asanāmeti vai matvā bharaṇe cāvicārite mokṣabhāve sthitaś cāpi dvandvībhūtaḥ parigrahe
english: He thought her name was not the same as his; and with the question of maintenance unresolved, being one who stood in a state of liberation, he was of two minds about accepting.

sanskrit: tato nāma sa kanyāyāḥ papraccha bhṛgunandana vāsuke bharaṇaṃ cāsyā na kuryām ity uvāca ha
english: Then he asked the name of the maiden, O joy of the Bhṛgu line, and he said to Vāsuki: "I will not maintain her."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca vāsukis tv abravīd vākyaṃ jaratkārum ṛṣiṃ tadā sanāmā tava kanyeyaṃ svasā me tapasānvitā
english: The Sūta said: Then Vāsuki spoke these words to the sage Jaratkāru: "This maiden is your namesake — she is my sister, endowed with austerities."

sanskrit: bhariṣyāmi ca te bhāryāṃ pratīcchemāṃ dvijottama rakṣaṇaṃ ca kariṣye 'syāḥ sarvaśaktyā tapodhana
english: "I will maintain your wife — accept her, O foremost of twice-born; and I will protect her with all my power, O treasure of austerity."

sanskrit: pratiśrute tu nāgena bhariṣye bhaginīm iti jaratkārus tadā veśma bhujagasya jagāma ha
english: When the serpent had promised "I will maintain my sister," Jaratkāru then went to the dwelling of the serpent.

sanskrit: tatra mantravidāṃ śreṣṭhas tapovṛddho mahāvrataḥ jagrāha pāṇiṃ dharmātmā vidhimantrapuraskṛtam
english: There, that foremost knower of mantras, great in austerity, of mighty vows, righteous-souled, took her hand according to the prescribed rites preceded by sacred formulas.
